spec_match.rationale: The zoom angle matches the spec's motivation, and supportedEntryTypes is probed correctly, but 'zoom' is simulated with the CSS zoom property (not real page zoom), and the 'reported in' readout is a UA sniff of Chrome/14[5-9] that misses Chrome 150+ and cannot actually observe the unit.

interactive.rationale: Zoom select, inject-shift, and reset all function, but the cumulative-CLS readout is unreliable: across three CDP runs one showed 0.0095 after the click and two stayed 0.0000, because the injected shift usually lands inside the hadRecentInput window and is discarded.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises the same shift at 100/150/200% zoom with a stable-in-CSS-pixels story — the spec's exact rationale.

edge_cases.rationale: Has a layout-shift-unsupported branch and multiple zoom levels, but no handling of hadRecentInput and no note that CSS zoom only approximates user zoom.

references.rationale: No chromestatus.com/feature/<id> link anywhere on the page — see-also lists only sibling concepts, breaking the invariant-3 self-heal contract.

conformance.rationale: Shares the structural feature suite (6/6 here); the zoom-stability claim itself has no assertion.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP-driven clicks with clean console on both viewports; the flaky cumulative-CLS behaviour was reproduced (one populated run, two zero runs), and the 'device pixels (likely);' readout — with its stray semicolon — was captured.

telemetry_health.rationale: Server-injected /public/demo-telemetry.js verified in the served DOM.

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout for stage, stats, and controls.

accessibility.rationale: Zoom select is wrapped in a label and buttons are native, but the stats grid is rebuilt via innerHTML with no live region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-measured clean at 360x740 (scrollWidth 360); desktop verified via screenshot.

openQuestions.title: Add the chromestatus feature link
openQuestions.detail: Invariant 3: every page must link chromestatus.com/feature/5155103518228480 so the slug self-heal can recover the folder. Add it to see-also.

openQuestions.title: Make the injected shift reliably observable
openQuestions.detail: The 80px height injection races the 500ms hadRecentInput window — CDP runs showed the cumulative CLS updating only occasionally. Delay the injection >500ms after the click with a countdown (shared fix with cls-demo and shift-reporter) so the zoom comparison actually accumulates a score every time.

openQuestions.title: Replace the Chrome/14[5-9] UA sniff
openQuestions.detail: The 'reported in' readout regexes the UA for Chrome/14[5-9], which stops matching at Chrome 150 and would then claim 'device pixels (likely)' forever; it also renders a stray trailing semicolon. Derive the message from a real signal where possible (e.g. compare a measured shift under DPR emulation) or at least parse the major version numerically.

summary: Good motivating angle (accessibility zoom) with a correct supportedEntryTypes probe, but three real defects: the chromestatus link is missing (invariant 3), the injected shift is usually swallowed by hadRecentInput (readout stayed 0.0000 in two of three CDP runs), and the version-sniffed 'reported in' label breaks at Chrome 150 and shows a typo semicolon. Browser-verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshot + DOM dump) and raw CDP (real click dispatch, console/network capture, 360x740 DPR3 mobile emulation) — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session. Chromium 141 predates Chrome 145, so v145-only API paths were validated on their fallback branches, not the new-API success path. The single failed fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet request is environmental (blocked host) and was not counted against any page.
